In the study of [[ancient Egyptian mathematics]], '''red auxiliary numbers''' are numbers written in red ink in the [[Rhind Mathematical Papyrus]], apparently used as aids for arithmetic computations involving [[fraction (mathematics)|fractions]]. It is considered to be the first examples of  method that uses [[least common multiple]]s.
